notes: Measured: with no .tp/local.json and >1 *.tasks.json, DiscoverTaskFile fails and unattended.go:230-235 compares a phantom empty override matching no file. Under TP_UNATTENDED=1, tp set --workflow --project audit_converge_on=blocking exits 2 in a tree where every base carries audit_converge_on:all (row 13's must-pass), and bases[0]=="" so no base is named. local.json is git-ignored, so a fresh clone or CI hits it. SKILL.md:196 and REFERENCE.md:338 promise naming that base unconditionally.

tp validate --project --strict exits 0 over an unreadable .tp/config.json (chmod 000 .tp: exit 0, skipped=[".tp/config.json"]), while the same tree readable exits 1 on the same audit_converge_on deviation. Under --quiet stderr is empty, so the only signal is an optional payload key. This file guards workflowDeviations and relOrSelf only; nothing guards runValidateProject's exit code. See validate_project.go:119-130 and 177-180.

version reads 0.36.1, ahead of the latest tag v0.36.0, so TestPluginVersionIsNotBehindTheLatestTag is green; unchanged from rounds 1 and 2. The release-time bump to 0.37.0 is still owed, and the field is load-bearing twice: the plugin update trigger and hooks/session-start.sh's minimum tp version. JSON is well-formed; no collection serializes as null.

Pins the --record sink: every offending line is named at once and the message lists the enum, so one bad file costs one round-trip. Nothing in this role's domain is wrong here. The gap is one sink upstream - tp audit --merge accepts the same out-of-enum category at exit 0 - and is recorded on the audit_merge.go row.

Measured: tp audit --merge accepts category:"banana" at exit 0 with a clean summary and writes it into merged.ndjson; tp audit <spec> --record merged.ndjson then exits 1. A guaranteed extra round-trip in the documented merge->record order. The record hint names a line number in the derived file, but dedupAuditRows re-sorts by (role,item_id), so the operator must map it back to the per-role input by hand. loadAuditMergeRows:174-187 validates only item_id and status.

Verified by running the binary, not only by reading: by_severity is absent on an all-PASS merge, present and correct on a mixed one, and survives --compact while overlap_report is dropped. All four unrecognised shapes (out-of-enum string, absent key, null, non-string) fold into one unrecognised bucket with no "" bucket. Map keys serialize sorted, so the payload is deterministic.

Both branches are covered - the converged arm and the clean-but-not-converged arm that a blocking cycle takes on every clean round - and each asserts the count renders as a numeral textually different from an empty round's. Targeted go test run is green. Nothing in this role's domain is wrong here.

Still open from round 2, re-measured: uncapped tp audit --status emits max_rounds:null and rounds_remaining:null but OMITS budget_exhausted entirely; capped emits all three. Its siblings in_flight_round and spec_coverage_clean_rounds both use an explicit null for the same not-applicable state. An agent reading payload["budget_exhausted"] fails on exactly the uncapped default (audit_max_rounds=0).

Nothing in this role's domain is wrong in the file itself. Note for the fix unit: TestAuditStatus_Shapes (124-154) asserts the empty-state payload key by key but never names budget_exhausted, max_rounds or rounds_remaining, which is why the uncapped key asymmetry on the audit_record.go row is unguarded by the one test that inspects this shape.

Row 18 is met properly: line 521 asserts the reversed --project write actually resolves to blocking rather than merely exiting 0, and lines 536-542 assert the fixture's premise (no severity key) beside the fail-closed rule. Note: the sibling helper fenceEnvelope (auditconvergeon_fence_test.go:844) works around errJSON parsing all of stderr; REFERENCE.md:27 does not document that the error envelope is stderr's last line.
